active_inquiry.goal_connection: The human objective requires at least 196 of 200 official episodes to complete an uninterrupted 2-second hold. This inquiry directly tests whether a fresh policy trained across the full 0.06-0.20 m radius range can achieve that behavior, while allocating failures among inner-radius distribution shift, target-angle and branch-limit geometry, maneuver timeout, and post-entry settling.
active_inquiry.handoff_conclusion: Observation from completed operation M1: a 2,088-point official-range grid found at least one joint-limit-valid inverse-kinematic branch for every target. The valid branch fraction was 0.9444, the minimum best-branch joint-limit margin was 12.33 degrees, and the minimum valid-branch Jacobian singular value was 0.0415. Compiled MuJoCo dynamics contain nonzero geom-derived masses and inertias, retain the authored 0.002 s timestep, 0.5 damping, 0.01 armature, and 5.0 actuator gear. Full-control open-loop probes produced initial joint accelerations of about 393-483 rad/s^2 and joint velocities of about 5.3-6.0 rad/s after ten 0.002 s substeps. These observations weaken the explanation that official failures are caused by unreachable targets or a generally weak actuator, and make braking/settling under 50 Hz action updates the leading physical capability concern. They do not establish closed-loop success: the torque probes were short and open-loop, did not use target-directed control, and did not measure tolerance interruptions or endpoint velocity during a hold. Branch selection remains consequential because 5.56% of sampled nominal branches were invalid and margins are angle-dependent. The omitted inner-radius training range, hidden hold phase, and actual learned-policy behavior remain untested. Thus the model's broad-reach consequence is supported, its stabilization concern is strengthened but not proven, and no claim about the 98% objective is yet justified.

This evaluation distinguishes the competing I1 mechanisms: first-entry and timeout statistics test maneuver capability, radius and angle plus branch-limit margins test geometric concentration, and first-entry, hold, interruption, velocity, and action diagnostics test post-entry settling under the 2-second uninterrupted criterion.

request.description: Allocate the 200-episode full-range evaluation failures by target radius, angle, joint-limit margin, maneuver timeout, and post-entry settling diagnostics.
request.rationale: M2 measured only 60% success, so the candidate is decisively below the 98% goal, but the durable result summary does not expose the per-episode distributions needed for a causal intervention. This analysis uses the complete M2 artifact to test whether failures are concentrated in inner-radius or angle/branch geometry, terminate before first entry, or enter tolerance and then fail the uninterrupted hold through interruptions and residual motion. request.rationale: M3 shows 78 of 80 failures are maneuver timeouts at radii 0.14-0.20 m, while the transferred policy already succeeds on 110 of 113 inner-band episodes and has only two post-entry failures overall. Concentrating training on the failed outer band tests whether the dominant deficit is hard-case allocation and maneuver learning rather than settling, branch feasibility, or insufficient hold shaping. The candidate will be evaluated on the unchanged full official distribution to measure any tradeoff against retained inner-band capability.

request.description: Evaluate the final transferred outer-band checkpoint on 200 fresh episodes from the unchanged official 0.06-0.20 m distribution with complete hold, geometry, timeout, and phase-aligned motion diagnostics.

measurements.label: T2 full-range transfer tradeoff and maneuver evaluation

request.rationale: T2 specialized the transferred T1 policy on 0.14-0.20 m, the band responsible for 78 of 80 M2 failures, but its training success remained only 0.15-0.17. A full official-range evaluation is the decisive check for whether this transfer preserved the strong 0.06-0.14 m capability while improving outer-band maneuver completion, or instead caused broad policy degradation through specialization or normalization mismatch. The observation already exposes both analytic IK branch errors; this bounded training change tests whether the failure concentration is primarily insufficient learning exposure to the seam-adjacent branch/angle geometries. Full official radius support and T3's 25% outer-radius oversampling are retained to avoid repeating T2's coverage loss. Restore T3's full-radius recipe with 25% outer-radius oversampling and uniform angle sampling as the validated baseline before changing observation or control representation.

request.rationale: M9 shows that T4's 50% seam-angle oversampling caused broad competence collapse: success fell to 18%, with 107 maneuver timeouts and 57 post-entry failures, including near-zero success in ordinary angle sectors. This rejects aggressive fresh distribution reweighting as the intervention. T3 remains the strongest behavioral baseline at 70.5% success with only 3 post-entry failures. A transfer run from T3 with a mild 10% hard-angle oversampling preserves the learned full-range controller and outer-radius competence while increasing exposure to the two dominant timeout sectors from M7. If this improves seam performance without reproducing T4's broad collapse, angle exposure is a contributing mechanism; if it does not, further sampling changes are not justified and the next intervention should alter target/branch representation or control shaping. All 153 episodes that entered tolerance completed the uninterrupted hold, so the remaining deficit remains maneuver entry rather than stabilization. Restore T5's 10% two-sided seam-angle transfer recipe as the strongest current behavioral baseline before changing the observation representation. The next intervention will address the likely discontinuity of wrapped scalar IK residuals at the target-angle seam, not further angle reweighting.

request.description: Train a fresh PPO policy using continuous sine/cosine encodings for all four analytic IK branch residuals, while retaining the validated T5 full-radius and mild seam-angle training distribution.
request.rationale: M13 shows that changing target-angle exposure did not solve the maneuver-entry deficit: T6 remained at 76.5%, with 26 of 28 positive-seam and 17 of 21 negative-seam episodes timing out, while every reached target completed the hold. The repeated seam localization despite different sampling interventions points to a representation/control discontinuity rather than insufficient exposure alone. The current observation wraps four analytic IK residuals to a scalar in [-pi, pi], creating a discontinuity precisely where target angles cross the +/-pi seam. Replace each scalar residual with its sine and cosine, preserving both open and folded branch information while making the representation continuous. Train fresh because the observation dimension changes from 11 to 15 and cannot safely reuse T5 weights. Retain T5's full-radius, 25% outer-radius, and 10% two-sided seam-angle sampling so the representation change is isolated from the rejected aggressive sampling recipes. Evaluation will test whether seam-sector maneuver timeouts fall without sacrificing ordinary-angle or radius performance.
